security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline backticks, and documented Claude skill paths. One destructive removal example is confirmed because it shows recursive deletion under the user home directory, which can remove local skill data if copied or modified incorrectly.

remediation.suggestion: Replace rm -rf examples with safer removal guidance, such as moving the skill directory to a temporary backup path or requiring an explicit confirmation step before deletion.

remediation.issue: Shell command examples are broad for a skill-management guide
remediation.suggestion: Mark command blocks as examples only and prefer read-only inspection commands unless a workflow requires file creation or removal.

content.value_statement: Teams often need a repeatable way to create and maintain Claude Agent Skills. This skill provides a practical guide for skill structure, metadata, sharing, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains where personal, project, and plugin skills are stored.
Shows the required SKILL.md frontmatter fields and naming rules.
Provides example single-file and multi-file skill layouts.
Describes allowed-tools usage for limiting skill capabilities.
Includes commands for listing, editing, sharing, and troubleshooting skills.
Offers a checklist for creating focused skills under recommended size limits.
limitations: It is a documentation guide, not an automated skill generator.
Some command examples can modify local files if copied directly.
It assumes Claude Code skill directory conventions.
It does not validate skills against a live marketplace schema.

use_cases.title: Create a personal workflow skill
use_cases.description: Use the guide to create a local skill directory, write SKILL.md, and define a clear trigger description.

use_cases.title: Share skills with a project team
use_cases.description: Follow the project skill layout and Git sharing steps so teammates receive the same workflow guidance.

use_cases.title: Debug skill activation issues
use_cases.description: Check descriptions, file paths, and YAML syntax when Claude does not select a skill as expected.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a focused Claude Agent Skill for [task]. Include a clear name, description, allowed tools, and a short usage example.

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SKILL.md for clarity, scope, trigger quality, and safe tool choices. Suggest only necessary changes.

prompt_templates.title: Organize project skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me organize project skills under .claude/skills. Recommend names, descriptions, and folder structure for these workflows: [list workflows].

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot skill selection
prompt_templates.prompt: Claude is not selecting my skill for this task: [task]. Inspect the skill description and structure, then explain what to change.

output_examples.input: I need a skill for writing Git commit messages.
output_examples.output: A focused commit-helper skill with a concise trigger description, read-only tool choices, and a checklist for summary and body formatting.

output_examples.input: Our team wants to share a code review skill.
output: Create the skill under the project skill directory.
Use a narrow description that mentions code review triggers.
Commit the skill folder so teammates receive it through Git.

output_examples.input: Claude is not using my skill.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting sequence that checks the trigger description, SKILL.md filename casing, YAML syntax, and overlap with other skills.

best_practices: Keep each skill focused on one workflow with a clear trigger description.
Use the smallest allowed-tools set that supports the skill purpose.
Include concrete examples and split long references into separate files.
anti_patterns: Do not create broad skills that cover unrelated workflows.
Do not give write or shell tools to read-only guidance skills.
Do not copy destructive shell examples without confirming the target path.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you create, update, test, and organize Claude Agent Skills for personal or team workflows.

faq.question: Does it create skills automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that you or Claude can follow when creating skill files.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The marketplace report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe for beginners?
faq.answer: Most guidance is safe, but users should be careful with shell examples that create, edit, or delete files.

faq.question: Can teams use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains project skill directories and Git sharing steps for team workflows.

faq.question: How should I choose allowed tools?
faq.answer: Choose only the tools the skill needs. Prefer read-only tools for review, search, and documentation tasks.
